messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 pager — authz anomaly: sudden sustained auth success rate from a compact IP set hitting Dedicated tenant acme-fin (eu-west-1). Pattern: same bearer token reused across ~150 distinct API keys, 09:15-09:28 UTC. Possible token replay/exfil. Alert IDs: A-3004506789, WAF-1013.

maya (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Starting live triage. Posting steps from runbook.

maya (oncall): Initial quick checks: are there any customer-facing 5xx errors? dashboards look OK for general latency but auth success count for acme-fin is +400% vs baseline.

leo (infra): Pulling session list now. Query I ran:
```
# ES query
GET /_search
{"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"tenant":"acme-fin"}},{"term":{"event":"auth_success"}},{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-30m"}}}]}}}
```
Found ~12k auth_success events in 13m, most from three /24s in eu-west-1.

sam (secops): If tokens are being replayed we should assume compromise. Recommend immediate actions: 1) create revocation plan for long-lived service tokens, 2) apply temporary WAF block for the offending CIDRs, 3) rotate any implicated service keys, and 4) start scoped S3 read access audit for acme-fin buckets.

irene (eng-sre): Agree. Two practical asks: can we do targeted key rotations to avoid broad user impact? Also we need to record customer impact before doing anything that could break their flows.

maya (oncall): Good point. Sam/Leo — can we identify which service principals the suspicious tokens map to? If it's a single integration we can rotate just that principal.

leo (infra): Correlating token IDs -> iam principal: mapping shows 3 token hashes mapping to service-account `svc-acme-ingest` and one to `svc-acme-legacy`. Both are long-lived.

sam (secops): Plan: 1) Temporarily block CIDRs at WAF to stop immediate replay (no customer-facing errors expected because this is unauthorized reuse). 2) Rotate `svc-acme-ingest` keys (create new keys, deploy short-lived credentials, update secrets), 3) Rotate `svc-acme-legacy` but do a canary with a single edge first. 4) Run S3 object access audit for last 72 hours.

jamal (cs): Heads-up — acme-fin has a high-value payments workload. If we rotate keys incorrectly we may cause transaction failures and they will page. I need ETA and an alternate contact line.

maya (oncall): ETA for WAF block: 5 minutes. ETA for ingest key rotation (create + staged rollout): 20 minutes. Will coordinate with Jamal for customer comms.

leo (infra): Blocking CIDRs now:
```
# waf-cli (internal)
waf block add --cidr 35.198.0.0/24 --reason "suspected token replay" --expires "+2h"
waf block add --cidr 52.17.128.0/24 --reason "suspected token replay" --expires "+2h"
```
ops-bot: waf block job started (job-id: job-3004506792).

ops-bot: waf block job completed (job-id: job-3004506792) :white_check_mark:.

maya (oncall): WAF blocks in place. Early metrics show auth_success rate for those CIDRs dropped to near zero. No increase in 5xx from acme-fin so far.

leo (infra): Generating new keys for svc-acme-ingest. Procedure: create key, update secret in vault, and set short TTL in deployment. Command fragment:
```
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-acme-ingest
vault kv put secret/acme-fin/svc-ingest access_key=AKIA... secret_key=...
# then trigger deploy to canary env
kubectl rollout restart deploy/acme-ingest-canary -n acme-fin
```

sam (secops): While keys are being swapped, start S3 audit:
```
# S3 access log grep (internal tooling)
search-logs --tenant acme-fin --service s3 --since 72h --pattern "GetObject" --out results.csv
```
And export any unusual client IPs for IOC.

irene (eng-sre): Noted. I'll monitor canary and watch error windows. If latency spikes or errors >1% we abort rotation rollback.

maya (oncall): Jamal — draft for customer inbound message:
"Hi team — we detected suspicious reuse of service tokens against your Dedicated environment. We're blocking suspicious traffic, rotating the implicated service credentials in a staged way, and running an audit of S3 accesses. We'll notify you if we need to take action that could impact traffic. Est. remediation window 30-60m. — Maya, Redwood Oncall"

jamal (cs): Good. Please mark all comms as high priority and include direct pager link. I'll prep legal & account exec.

ops-bot: key rotation job started (job-id: job-3004506821) for svc-acme-ingest.

ops-bot: key rotation job completed (job-id: job-3004506821) :white_check_mark:. New key staged in vault with TTL=1h.

leo (infra): Canary deploy picked up new creds and reports normal success rate. No failed auths observed on canary. Proceeding with progressive rollout to 25% -> 100% over next 15m.

maya (oncall): Rolling out to 25% now. Monitoring.

sam (secops): S3 audit initial results: 47 GetObject events from the suspect CIDRs across 6 objects in the last 72h. Objects looked like debug dumps (logs). Tagging as potential exfil. I'll open an internal case to preserve evidence.

maya (oncall): Because we found likely exfil of debug logs, escalating to Security incident classification SEC-INV-2026-003. Sam please take lead for evidence collection and legal notification.

sam (secops): On it. Collecting object manifests, snapshotting S3 access logs, and requesting KMS key rotation discussion.

jamal (cs): Customer notified via email + phone alert with the drafted message. They asked for an immediate list of rotated keys and a short postmortem timeframe. I'll update them after we confirm all rotations succeed.

irene (eng-sre): 25% roll to 50% now. Metrics steady. No client errors observed.

ops-bot: progressive rollout 50% complete (roll-id roll-3004506890).

maya (oncall): 100% rollout complete. All implicated tokens rotated. WAF blocks will stay for 2h and then be reviewed.

leo (infra): Running quick inventory of other long-lived service accounts for acme-fin; found 2 more with >90d keys. I'll schedule rotation recommendations and create a short-lived creds policy for the tenant.

sam (secops): Evidence bundle stored: s3://sec-evidence/SEC-INV-2026-003/, snapshot_id=evid-3004506955. Legal & IR cc'd.

maya (oncall): Summary for incident channel:
- Cause: suspected token replay/exfil using long-lived svc-acme-ingest keys, likely from leaked debug logs.
- Impact: no customer-facing outage observed; potential data exposure of debug logs for acme-fin.
- Actions taken: WAF CIDR blocks, rotated svc-acme-ingest & svc-acme-legacy (progressive), S3 access audit, evidence collected, customer notified.
- Next steps: full postmortem (owners: sam/leo/irene), KMS rotation review, recommend tenant policy change to short-lived creds.

jamal (cs): Thanks — I'll schedule customer follow-up for 3 hours and request a technical summary for them.

maya (oncall): Handing off to Sam for secops lead and Leo for infra follow-up. I'll put this to monitoring watch and move to incident standby. If anything regresses ping me directly. :lock:

sam (secops): Taking lead. Adding SES/legal/IR, will coordinate postmortem.

ops-bot: incident status changed to monitoring (incident-id: A-3004506789).

maya (oncall): Closing out on-call shift notes: see runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-replay-triage for details, and incident doc SEC-INV-2026-003 in tracker.
